text:
Jesper Bratt is doing everything except scoring. He has 23 points in 25 games for New Jersey, 19 of them assists, but only 4 goals on 6.5 expected goals (the quality of his chances), and he's shooting 7.4% against a talent range centred around 12%. That's the clearest "due" flag in his profile: he keeps getting the looks, and goals tend to follow chances.

The rest of his game is in top form. The Devils take 62% of the expected goals with him on at five on five, almost eight points better than without him, and his team has scored 4.2 fewer goals than expected with him out there, so his assist total is, if anything, held down too. Evolving-Hockey rated him 98th percentile at driving offense last season against the other team's best players.

The bigger picture: a 162nd overall pick came into this season with 518 career points, and The Hockey News' Mike Fink is already wondering how close he'll get to Patrik Elias. Watch the shooting percentage. It is the one number between him and a star-level season.
headline: Bratt's goals are coming, the chances say so
